gen-gf-autour-one-gf-noto-sans-bamum: Expressive and bold, Autour One draws every curve with a clear channel running into the round letters and no shift in line width. And Noto Sans Bamum does the opposite job, keeping its small letters wide open with curved strokes that stop before they turn inward.
gen-gf-autour-one-gf-noto-sans-bassa-vah: Noto Sans Bassa Vah has a dominant midsection that swallows most of the line's height, with a jaw-open c. Autour One joins it with cut-out strokes of fixed width, so the heading looks routed while the plain sans looks relaxed.
gen-gf-autour-one-gf-noto-sans-batak: Noto Sans Batak reads big and friendly, its x-height towering and its e wide open instead of squeezed shut. Autour One's ribbon-cut stroke ends give it a bolder edge.
gen-gf-autour-one-gf-noto-sans-bengali: Autour One's ruler-drawn line keeps a constant width from stem to curve, with a minimal step down from capitals. But Noto Sans Bengali, a plain sans, loosens things with distinctly open letter mouths and capitals barely taller than its lowercase.
gen-gf-autour-one-gf-noto-sans-bhaiksuki: Round, rope-tight, and loud. Autour One has no contrast between stems and joins. Noto Sans Bhaiksuki answers in a sans-serif with swollen lowercase and apertures that stay easy to read, so the heading shouts while the text speaks plainly.
gen-gf-autour-one-gf-noto-sans-brahmi: Autour One's o is a ring with a constant wall, and every round letter gets a clear channel leading in. Then Noto Sans Brahmi, a plain sans, sets its mean line high and leaves each curve open-ended, giving the heading bold space to breathe against.
gen-gf-autour-one-gf-noto-sans-buhid: Chunky joins, no thinning. Autour One keeps its strokes full where they meet. Noto Sans Buhid, a plain sans with generous space between curve ends and the stem, and a high-set x-height, gives text a steady, unhurried pace.
gen-gf-autour-one-gf-noto-sans-carian: Autour One's t has a crossbar and stem of one width. Noto Sans Carian is the one to scale up when text feels small, since its terminals stay apart like open scissor blades and tiny gaps separate ascender tops from the x-height line.
gen-gf-autour-one-gf-noto-sans-chakma: Approachable at heart, Autour One draws with a plotter-pen single-weight line. Noto Sans Chakma, a plain sans packing lowercase up toward the caps, leaves the s and c uncrowded, so bumping its size a notch helps text hold its own.
gen-gf-autour-one-gf-noto-sans-cham: Noto Sans Cham reads modern and clean, with open c shapes giving plenty of entry space and tall rounded lowercase forms. And Autour One, with zero stroke contrast throughout, sits above it as a bold sans-serif counterpart.
